raw: CHAPTER V. The Jackal
en: [Chapter 5]

raw: Those were drinking days, and most men drank hard.
en: The Jackal Those were drinking days, and most men drank heavily.
ko: 자칼. 그때는 술의 시대였고, 대부분의 남자들은 술을 몹시 많이 마셨다.

raw: So very great is the improvement Time has brought about in such habits, that a moderate statement of the quantity of wine and punch which one man would swallow in the course of a night, without any detriment to his reputation as a perfect gentleman, would seem, in these days, a ridiculous exaggeration.
en: Time has improved these habits so much that a moderate description of those drinking sessions would seem ridiculous today. Back then, a man could drink a huge amount of wine and punch in a night without hurting his reputation as a gentleman.
ko: 시간이 흘러 이러한 습관들이 많이 개선되었기에, 당시의 술자리 모습을 적당히 묘사하는 것조차 오늘날에는 우스꽝스럽게 보일 것이다. 그 시절에는 하룻밤에 엄청난 양의 포도주와 펀치 술을 마셔도 신사로서의 명성에 흠이 가지 않았다.

raw: The learned profession of the law was certainly not behind any other learned profession in its Bacchanalian propensities; neither was Mr.
en: The legal profession was certainly not behind any other in its drinking habits; nor was Mr.
ko: 법조계 종사자들의 음주 습관은 다른 어떤 직업군에도 결코 뒤지지 않았으며, 다음 사람 역시 마찬가지였다.

raw: Stryver, already fast shouldering his way to a large and lucrative practice, behind his compeers in this particular, any more than in the drier parts of the legal race.
en: Stryver, who was already aggressively pushing his way toward a large and profitable legal practice, wasn't trailing behind his peers in this area any more than he was in the more boring parts of the legal profession.
ko: 크고 수익성 높은 법률 업무를 향해 이미 공격적으로 밀어붙이고 있던 스트라이버는, 법조계의 더 지루한 분야에서 그랬던 것처럼 이 부분에서도 동료들에게 결코 뒤처지지 않았다.

raw: A favourite at the Old Bailey, and eke at the Sessions, Mr.
en: As a favorite at the Old Bailey and other courts, Mr.
ko: 올드 베일리와 다른 법원들에서 총애를 받던 인물로서,

raw: Stryver had begun cautiously to hew away the lower staves of the ladder on which he mounted.
en: Stryver had begun to carefully secure his path to success.
ko: 스트라이버는 자신의 성공 가도를 조심스럽게 확보하기 시작했다.

raw: Sessions and Old Bailey had now to summon their favourite, specially, to their longing arms; and shouldering itself towards the visage of the Lord Chief Justice in the Court of King’s Bench, the florid countenance of Mr.
en: The criminal courts at the Sessions and Old Bailey now had to send special requests for their favorite lawyer. And the red face of Mr. Stryver was constantly pushing its way forward to be seen by the Lord Chief Justice in the Court of King's Bench.
ko: 순회 재판소와 올드 베일리의 형사 법원들은 이제 그들이 가장 좋아하는 변호사를 모시기 위해 특별한 요청을 보내야만 했다. 그리고 스트라이버 씨의 붉은 얼굴은 왕립 재판소의 대법원장 눈에 띄기 위해 끊임없이 앞으로 밀고 나아가고 있었다.

raw: Stryver might be daily seen, bursting out of the bed of wigs, like a great sunflower pushing its way at the sun from among a rank garden-full of flaring companions.
en: Stryver's red face could be seen in the King's Bench court, standing out among the other lawyers' wigs like a large sunflower pushing its way up in a crowded garden.
ko: 스트라이버의 붉은 얼굴은 왕립 재판소에서 다른 변호사들의 가발 사이로 눈에 띄게 보였는데, 마치 빽빽한 정원에서 위로 솟아오르는 커다란 해바라기 같았다.

raw: It had once been noted at the Bar, that while Mr.
en: Other lawyers had once noted that Mr.
ko: 다른 변호사들은 예전에 다음과 같이 지적한 적이 있었다.

raw: Stryver was a glib man, and an unscrupulous, and a ready, and a bold, he had not that faculty of extracting the essence from a heap of statements, which is among the most striking and necessary of the advocate’s accomplishments.
en: Stryver was quick-tongued, bold, and ready. But they also noted that he lacked the ability to find the core facts in a pile of documents. This was a key skill for a lawyer.
ko: 스트라이버는 달변가에 대담하고 준비성이 철저했다. 그러나 그들은 또한 그가 서류 더미에서 핵심 사실을 찾아내는 능력이 부족하다는 점도 지적했다. 이는 변호사에게 필수적인 기술이었다.

raw: But, a remarkable improvement came upon him as to this.
en: However, he had improved remarkably in this.
ko: 그러나 그는 이 부분에서 눈에 띄게 발전했다.

raw: The more business he got, the greater his power seemed to grow of getting at its pith and marrow; and however late at night he sat carousing with Sydney Carton, he always had his points at his fingers’ ends in the morning.
en: The more work he got, the better he became at finding the main points of a case. No matter how late he sat drinking with Sydney Carton, he always had the facts ready by morning.
ko: 일이 많아질수록 그는 사건의 요점을 파악하는 능력이 더 좋아졌다. 그가 시드니 카턴과 아무리 늦게까지 술을 마셔도, 그는 항상 아침이면 사실관계를 완벽히 준비해 놓았다.

raw: Sydney Carton, idlest and most unpromising of men, was Stryver’s great ally.
en: Sydney Carton, the idlest and most unpromising of men, was Stryver’s great ally.
ko: 가장 게으르고 앞날이 캄캄한 사내인 시드니 카턴은 스트라이버의 훌륭한 동맹이었다.

raw: What the two drank together, between Hilary Term and Michaelmas, might have floated a king’s ship.
en: The amount the two drank together between law terms could have floated a battleship.
ko: 그 두 사람이 재판 휴정기 동안 함께 마신 술의 양은 전함을 띄울 수 있을 정도였다.

raw: Stryver never had a case in hand, anywhere, but Carton was there, with his hands in his pockets, staring at the ceiling of the court; they went the same Circuit, and even there they prolonged their usual orgies late into the night, and Carton was rumoured to be seen at broad day, going home stealthily and unsteadily to his lodgings, like a dissipated cat.
en: Stryver never had a case without Carton being there, hands in his pockets, staring at the ceiling. They traveled the same court circuits together, staying up late drinking. Carton was rumored to be seen at dawn, walking unsteadily back to his lodgings like a stray cat.
ko: 스트라이버가 맡은 사건에는 항상 카턴이 주머니에 손을 넣고 천장을 바라보며 곁에 있었다. 그들은 같은 순회 재판을 함께 다니며 늦게까지 깨어 술을 마셨다. 카턴은 새벽녘에 마치 길 잃은 고양이처럼 비틀거리며 자신의 하숙집으로 돌아가는 모습이 목격된다는 소문이 돌았다.

raw: At last, it began to get about, among such as were interested in the matter, that although Sydney Carton would never be a lion, he was an amazingly good jackal, and that he rendered suit and service to Stryver in that humble capacity.
en: Eventually, those in the legal world realized that while Carton would never be the famous leader, the "lion", he was an excellent helper, a "jackal," doing the hard background work for Stryver.
ko: 결국 법조계 사람들은 카턴이 결코 유명한 지도자인 사자가 될 수는 없겠지만, 스트라이버를 위해 힘든 뒷바라지를 하는 훌륭한 조력자 즉 자칼이라는 사실을 깨달았다.

raw: “Ten o’clock, sir,” said the man at the tavern, whom he had charged to wake him--“ten o’clock, sir.”
en: "Ten o'clock, sir," said the tavern worker who had been ordered to wake Carton. "Ten o'clock, sir."
ko: 카턴을 깨우라고 지시받았던 술집 종업원이 말했다. '10시입니다, 손님. 10시요.'

raw: “_What’s_ the matter?”
en: "_What's_ the matter?"
ko: '무슨 일이야?'

raw: “Ten o’clock, sir.”
en: "Ten o'clock, sir."
ko: '10시입니다, 손님.'

raw: “What do you mean?
en: "What do you mean?
ko: '무슨 소리야?

raw: Ten o’clock at night?”
en: Ten o'clock at night?"
ko: 밤 10시라고?'

raw: “Yes, sir.
en: "Yes, sir.
ko: '네, 손님.

raw: Your honour told me to call you.”
en: You told me to wake you."
ko: 깨워달라고 하셨잖아요.'

raw: “Oh!
en: "Oh!

raw: I remember.
en: I remember.
ko: 기억났어.

raw: Very well, very well.”
en: Very well, very well."
ko: 알았어, 알았다고.'

raw: After a few dull efforts to get to sleep again, which the man dexterously combated by stirring the fire continuously for five minutes, he got up, tossed his hat on, and walked out.
en: After trying to fall back asleep, Carton got up. The worker had prevented him from sleeping by stirring the fire for five minutes. He put on his hat and walked out.
ko: 다시 잠들려다 실패한 카턴은 일어났다. 종업원이 5분 동안 난로 불을 뒤적거리는 바람에 잘 수가 없었다. 그는 모자를 쓰고 밖으로 걸어 나갔다.

raw: He turned into the Temple, and, having revived himself by twice pacing the pavements of King’s Bench-walk and Paper-buildings, turned into the Stryver chambers.
en: He walked to the Temple district, clearing his head by walking around King's Bench Walk and Paper Buildings twice, before entering Stryver's offices.
ko: 그는 템플 구역으로 걸어가며 머리를 맑게 하기 위해 킹스 벤치 워크와 페이퍼 빌딩스 주변을 두 바퀴 돈 후 스트라이버의 사무실로 들어갔다.

raw: The Stryver clerk, who never assisted at these conferences, had gone home, and the Stryver principal opened the door.
en: Stryver's clerk had already gone home, so Stryver himself opened the door.
ko: 스트라이버의 서기는 이미 퇴근했기 때문에, 스트라이버가 직접 문을 열어주었다.

raw: He had his slippers on, and a loose bed-gown, and his throat was bare for his greater ease.
en: He was wearing slippers and a loose robe, with his collar open for comfort.
ko: 그는 편하게 슬리퍼를 신고 헐렁한 가운을 걸친 채 옷깃을 풀어 헤치고 있었다.

raw: He had that rather wild, strained, seared marking about the eyes, which may be observed in all free livers of his class, from the portrait of Jeffries downward, and which can be traced, under various disguises of Art, through the portraits of every Drinking Age.
en: He had that wild, exhausted, and burned-out look around his eyes that you can see in all heavy drinkers of his social class. You can spot it in historical portraits of famous partiers from years past, hiding under different artistic styles throughout every age of heavy drinking.
ko: 그의 눈가에는 그와 같은 사회적 지위를 가진 애주가들에게서 흔히 볼 수 있는 거칠고 지치고 기진맥진한 기색이 역력했다. 그것은 과거 유명한 파티광들의 역사적 초상화에서도 찾을 수 있는데, 모든 시대의 과음의 역사 속에서 다양한 예술 양식 아래 숨겨져 있다.

raw: “You are a little late, Memory,” said Stryver.
en: "You are a little late, Memory," said Stryver.
ko: '조금 늦었군, 메모리,' 스트라이버가 말했다.

raw: “About the usual time; it may be a quarter of an hour later.”
en: "About the usual time; maybe fifteen minutes late."
ko: '늘 오던 시간이야. 15분 정도 늦었나.'

raw: They went into a dingy room lined with books and littered with papers, where there was a blazing fire.
en: They went into a dusty room lined with books and messy papers, where a fire was burning.
ko: 그들은 책과 지저분한 서류가 늘어서 있고 불이 피워져 있는 먼지투성이의 방으로 들어갔다.

raw: A kettle steamed upon the hob, and in the midst of the wreck of papers a table shone, with plenty of wine upon it, and brandy, and rum, and sugar, and lemons.
en: A kettle steamed on the stove. On a cleared table sat plenty of wine, brandy, rum, sugar, and lemons.
ko: 난로 위에서는 주전자가 김을 내뿜고 있었다. 말끔히 치워진 탁자 위에는 와인, 브랜디, 럼, 설탕, 레몬이 잔뜩 놓여 있었다.

raw: “You have had your bottle, I perceive, Sydney.”
en: "I see you've had your bottle already, Sydney."
ko: '이미 한 병 비웠나 보군, 시드니.'

raw: “Two to-night, I think.
en: "Two tonight, I think.
ko: '오늘 밤엔 두 병인 것 같아.

raw: I have been dining with the day’s client; or seeing him dine--it’s all one!”
en: I dined with today's client, or watched him dine, it's the same thing!"
ko: 오늘 의뢰인이랑 같이 저녁을 먹었지. 아니, 그가 먹는 걸 구경했다고 해야 하나. 똑같은 얘기야!'

raw: “That was a rare point, Sydney, that you brought to bear upon the identification.
en: "That was a great point you made, Sydney, about the resemblance and the identification.
ko: '시드니, 자네가 그 닮은꼴과 신원 확인에 대해 지적한 부분은 정말 훌륭했어.

raw: How did you come by it?
en: How did you think of it?
ko: 어떻게 그런 생각을 해냈지?

raw: When did it strike you?”
en: When did it occur to you?"
ko: 언제 그 생각이 떠오른 거야?'

raw: “I thought he was rather a handsome fellow, and I thought I should have been much the same sort of fellow, if I had had any luck.”
en: "I thought he was a handsome fellow, and I realized I would have looked just like him if I had had any luck in life."
ko: '잘생긴 녀석이라고 생각했는데, 내 인생에 운이 조금만 따라줬더라도 나도 딱 저렇게 생겼겠구나 싶더라고.'

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.
ko: 미스터

raw: Stryver laughed till he shook his precocious paunch.
en: Stryver laughed so hard his stomach shook.
ko: 스트라이버는 배가 출렁일 정도로 크게 웃었다.

raw: “You and your luck, Sydney!
en: "You and your luck, Sydney!
ko: '자네와 자네의 그 운이란, 시드니!

raw: Get to work, get to work.”
en: Let's get to work, get to work."
ko: 이제 일이나 하자고, 일하자고.'

raw: Sullenly enough, the jackal loosened his dress, went into an adjoining room, and came back with a large jug of cold water, a basin, and a towel or two.
en: Sullenly, the jackal loosened his collar and went to the next room. He returned with a large jug of cold water, a basin, and a few towels.
ko: 자칼은 뚱한 표정으로 옷깃을 풀고 옆방으로 갔다. 그는 차가운 물이 가득 담긴 큰 주전자와 대야, 수건 몇 장을 가지고 돌아왔다.

raw: Steeping the towels in the water, and partially wringing them out, he folded them on his head in a manner hideous to behold, sat down at the table, and said, “Now I am ready!”
en: Soaking the towels in the water and wringing them out slightly, he wrapped them around his head in a strange, ugly way. He sat at the table and said, "Now I'm ready!"
ko: 그는 수건을 물에 적시고 가볍게 짠 다음, 머리에 이상하고 우스꽝스러운 모양으로 둘렀다. 그는 탁자에 앉아 말했다. '이제 준비됐어!'

raw: “Not much boiling down to be done to-night, Memory,” said Mr.
en: "Not too much work to summarize tonight, Memory," said Mr.
ko: '오늘 밤엔 요약할 일이 그리 많지 않아, 메모리,' 미스터

raw: Stryver, gaily, as he looked among his papers.
en: Stryver cheerfully, looking through his papers.
ko: 스트라이버가 서류를 훑어보며 기분 좋게 말했다.

raw: “How much?”
en: "How much?"
ko: '얼마나 되는데?'

raw: “Only two sets of them.”
en: "Only two cases."
ko: '두 사건뿐이야.'

raw: “Give me the worst first.”
en: "Give me the harder one first."
ko: '어려운 것부터 줘.'

raw: “There they are, Sydney.
en: "Here they are, Sydney.
ko: '여기 있네, 시드니.

raw: Fire away!”
en: Go ahead!"
ko: 시작해!'

raw: The lion then composed himself on his back on a sofa on one side of the drinking-table, while the jackal sat at his own paper-bestrewn table proper, on the other side of it, with the bottles and glasses ready to his hand.
en: The "lion" then lay back on a sofa on one side of the table, while the "jackal" sat at his own messy desk on the other side, with bottles and glasses nearby.
ko: 그러고 나서 '사자'는 탁자 한쪽의 소파에 기대 누웠고, '자칼'은 반대편에 있는 자신의 지저분한 책상에 앉았다. 그의 주변에는 병과 유리잔들이 놓여 있었다.

raw: Both resorted to the drinking-table without stint, but each in a different way; the lion for the most part reclining with his hands in his waistband, looking at the fire, or occasionally flirting with some lighter document; the jackal, with knitted brows and intent face, so deep in his task, that his eyes did not even follow the hand he stretched out for his glass--which often groped about, for a minute or more, before it found the glass for his lips.
en: Both drank constantly, but in different ways. Stryver lay back with his hands on his belt, staring at the fire or occasionally looking at a document. Carton worked with a worried frown and a focused face. He was so deep in his work that he didn't even look up when reaching for his glass.
ko: 두 사람은 끊임없이 술을 마셨지만, 방식은 달랐다. 스트라이버는 벨트 위에 손을 얹은 채 누워서 불을 멍하니 바라보거나 이따금 서류를 쳐다보았다. 카턴은 이마를 찌푸리고 집중한 얼굴로 일했다. 그는 일에 너무 깊이 빠져 있어서 술잔을 집을 때조차 고개를 들지 않았다.

raw: Two or three times, the matter in hand became so knotty, that the jackal found it imperative on him to get up, and steep his towels anew.
en: Two or three times, the legal case they were working on became so complicated that the "jackal" had to get up and soak his towels in cold water all over again.
ko: 두세 번쯤, 그들이 작업하던 법률 사건이 너무 복잡해져서 '자칼'은 자리에서 일어나 수건을 찬물에 다시 적셔야 했다.

raw: From these pilgrimages to the jug and basin, he returned with such eccentricities of damp headgear as no words can describe; which were made the more ludicrous by his anxious gravity.
en: Two or three times, the work became so difficult that Carton had to get up and soak his towels again, returning with damp headgear that looked ridiculous despite his serious expression.
ko: 두세 번쯤, 일이 너무 어려워져서 카턴은 자리에서 일어나 수건을 다시 적셔야 했고, 진지한 표정에도 불구하고 우스꽝스러워 보이는 축축한 머리 장식을 하고 돌아왔다.

raw: At length the jackal had got together a compact repast for the lion, and proceeded to offer it to him.
en: Finally, the jackal had put together a neat little package of information for the lion, and he handed it over for him to digest.
ko: 마침내 자칼은 사자가 소화할 수 있도록 정보를 작고 깔끔하게 정리하여 넘겨주었다.

raw: The lion took it with care and caution, made his selections from it, and his remarks upon it, and the jackal assisted both.
en: Stryver went over the notes carefully, making remarks and adjustments with Carton's help.
ko: 스트라이버는 카턴의 도움을 받아 의견을 내고 수정하며 메모를 주의 깊게 검토했다.

raw: When the repast was fully discussed, the lion put his hands in his waistband again, and lay down to meditate.
en: When they had fully discussed all the information, the lion tucked his hands back into his waistband and lay down to think deeply about it.
ko: 모든 정보에 대한 논의를 마친 후, 사자는 다시 허리춤에 손을 넣고 누워서 깊이 생각에 잠겼다.

raw: The jackal then invigorated himself with a bumper for his throttle, and a fresh application to his head, and applied himself to the collection of a second meal; this was administered to the lion in the same manner, and was not disposed of until the clocks struck three in the morning.
en: Meanwhile, Carton drank another glass, adjusted his head towels, and began working on the second case. They did not finish until the clocks struck three in the morning.
ko: 그동안 카턴은 술을 한 잔 더 마시고 머리에 두른 수건을 고쳐 쓴 뒤 두 번째 사건에 착수했다. 그들은 새벽 3시가 되어서야 일을 마쳤다.

raw: “And now we have done, Sydney, fill a bumper of punch,” said Mr.
en: "And now that we are done, Sydney, pour us a glass of punch," said Mr.
ko: '이제 일도 끝났으니, 시드니, 우리 펀치 한 잔 따르지,' 미스터

raw: Stryver.
en: Stryver.
ko: 스트라이버가 말했다.

raw: The jackal removed the towels from his head, which had been steaming again, shook himself, yawned, shivered, and complied.
en: Carton took the steaming towels off his head. He shook himself, yawned, shivered, and poured the drinks.
ko: 카턴은 김이 나는 수건을 머리에서 벗었다. 그는 몸을 털고 하품을 한 뒤 몸을 부르르 떨며 술을 따랐다.

raw: “You were very sound, Sydney, in the matter of those crown witnesses to-day.
en: "You were very sharp about those prosecution witnesses today, Sydney.
ko: '오늘 검찰 측 증인들에 대한 자네의 대응은 아주 날카로웠어, 시드니.

raw: Every question told.”
en: Every question hit its mark."
ko: 모든 질문이 정곡을 찔렀지.'

raw: “I always am sound; am I not?”
en: "I am always sharp, aren't I?"
ko: '난 항상 날카롭지 않아?'

raw: “I don’t gainsay it.
en: "I don't deny it.
ko: '부정하진 않겠어.

raw: What has roughened your temper?
en: But what has put you in such a bad mood?
ko: 근데 왜 그렇게 기분이 안 좋은 거야?

raw: Put some punch to it and smooth it again.”
en: Have some punch and cheer up."
ko: 펀치 좀 마시고 기운 내라고.'

raw: With a deprecatory grunt, the jackal again complied.
en: With a grunt of protest, Carton drank.
ko: 카턴은 투덜거리듯 소리를 내며 술을 마셨다.

raw: “The old Sydney Carton of old Shrewsbury School,” said Stryver, nodding his head over him as he reviewed him in the present and the past, “the old seesaw Sydney.
en: "You are the same Sydney Carton from our old school days," said Stryver, looking at him.
ko: '자네는 학창 시절의 그 시드니 카턴 그대로군,' 스트라이버가 그를 쳐다보며 말했다.

raw: Up one minute and down the next; now in spirits and now in despondency!”
en: "Always going up and down, happy one minute and depressed the next."
ko: '항상 기복이 심해서, 어느 순간엔 기뻐했다가 다음 순간엔 우울해지지.'

raw: “Ah!” returned the other, sighing: “yes!
en: "Ah!" Carton sighed.
ko: '아!' 카턴이 한숨을 쉬었다.

raw: The same Sydney, with the same luck.
en: "Yes, the same Sydney with the same bad luck.
ko: '그래, 예전과 똑같이 운 없는 그 시드니지.

raw: Even then, I did exercises for other boys, and seldom did my own.”
en: Even back then, I did the homework for other boys and neglected my own."
ko: 그때도 난 다른 애들 숙제나 해주고 정작 내 것은 소홀히 했잖아.'

raw: “And why not?”
en: "And why did you do that?"
ko: '대체 왜 그랬던 거야?'

raw: “God knows.
en: "God knows.
ko: '신만이 아시겠지.

raw: It was my way, I suppose.”
en: It was just my way, I suppose."
ko: 그게 그냥 내 방식이었나 봐.'

raw: He sat, with his hands in his pockets and his legs stretched out before him, looking at the fire.
en: He sat with his hands in his pockets and his legs stretched out, staring at the fire.
ko: 그는 주머니에 손을 넣고 다리를 뻗은 채 앉아서 불을 멍하니 바라보았다.

raw: “Carton,” said his friend, squaring himself at him with a bullying air, as if the fire-grate had been the furnace in which sustained endeavour was forged, and the one delicate thing to be done for the old Sydney Carton of old Shrewsbury School was to shoulder him into it, “your way is, and always was, a lame way.
en: "Carton," his friend said, squaring up to him with a bullying attitude. He looked as if the fireplace was a furnace where hard work was made, and the only way to help his old school friend Sydney Carton was to shove him right into it. "Your way of doing things is, and always has been, a weak way."
ko: '카턴,' 그의 친구가 위압적인 태도로 그를 정면으로 바라보며 말했다. 그는 마치 벽난로가 힘든 노력이 만들어지는 용광로이며, 그의 옛 학교 친구 시드니 카턴을 돕는 유일한 방법은 그를 바로 그 안으로 밀어 넣는 것뿐이라는 듯한 표정이었다. '자네의 일 처리 방식은 항상 나약했어.'

raw: You summon no energy and purpose.
en: You have no energy or purpose.
ko: 자네에겐 활력도 목적도 없어.

raw: Look at me.”
en: Look at me."
ko: 나를 보라고.'

raw: “Oh, botheration!” returned Sydney, with a lighter and more good-humoured laugh, “don’t _you_ be moral!”
en: "Oh, stop it!" Sydney laughed, sounding more cheerful. "Don't start preaching to _me_!"
ko: '아, 그만해!' 시드니가 좀 더 밝아진 목소리로 웃으며 말했다. '나한테 설교하려 들지 마!'

raw: “How have I done what I have done?” said Stryver; “how do I do what I do?”
en: "How do you think I got to where I am?" Stryver asked. "How do I do it?"
ko: '내가 어떻게 지금의 자리에 올랐다고 생각하나?' 스트라이버가 물었다. '내가 어떻게 그럴 수 있었지?'

raw: “Partly through paying me to help you, I suppose.
en: "Partly by paying me to help you, I suppose.
ko: '어느 정도는 나한테 돈을 주고 도움을 받았기 때문이겠지.

raw: But it’s not worth your while to apostrophise me, or the air, about it; what you want to do, you do.
en: But there's no need to lecture me; what you want to do, you do.
ko: 하지만 나한테 설교할 필요는 없어. 넌 네가 하고 싶은 걸 하잖아.

raw: You were always in the front rank, and I was always behind.”
en: You were always in the lead, and I was always behind."
ko: 넌 항상 앞서 나갔고, 난 늘 뒤처졌지.'

raw: “I had to get into the front rank; I was not born there, was I?”
en: "I had to work to get to the front; I wasn't born there, was I?"
ko: '앞서가려면 노력해야 했어. 내가 날 때부터 그 자리에 있던 건 아니잖아?'

raw: “I was not present at the ceremony; but my opinion is you were,” said Carton. At this, he laughed again, and they both laughed.
en: "I wasn't there to see it, but I bet you were," Carton said, and they both laughed.
ko: '내가 본 건 아니지만, 그랬을 거라고 장담해,' 카턴이 말했고, 두 사람은 함께 웃었다.

raw: “Before Shrewsbury, and at Shrewsbury, and ever since Shrewsbury,”  pursued Carton, “you have fallen into your rank, and I have fallen into mine.
en: "Before school, at school, and ever since," Carton continued. "You have taken your place, and I have taken mine.
ko: '입학 전에도, 학교 다닐 때도, 그리고 그 이후로도 쭉,' 카턴이 계속해서 말했다. '넌 네 자리를 차지했고, 난 내 자리를 차지했지.

raw: Even when we were fellow-students in the Student-Quarter of Paris, picking up French, and French law, and other French crumbs that we didn’t get much good of, you were always somewhere, and I was always nowhere.”
en: Even when we were students in Paris, learning French and French law, you were always succeeding and I was always getting nowhere."
ko: 우리가 파리에서 학생 시절 프랑스어와 프랑스 법을 배울 때도 넌 항상 성공했고 난 늘 제자리걸음이었어.'

raw: “And whose fault was that?”
en: "And whose fault was that?"
ko: '그게 누구 잘못이었지?'

raw: “Upon my soul, I am not sure that it was not yours.
en: "Honestly, I think it was yours.
ko: '솔직히, 네 잘못인 것 같아.

raw: You were always driving and riving and shouldering and passing, to that restless degree that I had no chance for my life but in rust and repose.
en: You were always so busy pushing and shouldering your way forward that I had no choice but to sit back and rest.
ko: 네가 늘 앞으로 밀치고 어깨싸움을 하며 나아가느라 바빴기 때문에, 난 뒤에 앉아서 쉴 수밖에 없었거든.

raw: It’s a gloomy thing, however, to talk about one’s own past, with the day breaking.
en: But it's depressing to talk about the past at dawn.
ko: 하지만 새벽부터 옛날이야기를 하는 건 우울해.

raw: Turn me in some other direction before I go.”
en: Change the subject before I go."
ko: 나 가기 전에 주제나 바꾸자고.'

raw: “Well then!
en: "Well then!
ko: '그렇다면!

raw: Pledge me to the pretty witness,” said Stryver, holding up his glass. “Are you turned in a pleasant direction?”
en: Let's toast the pretty witness," said Stryver, raising his glass. "Is that a better subject?"
ko: 그 예쁜 증인을 위해 건배나 하지,' 스트라이버가 잔을 들며 말했다. '이건 좀 나은 주제인가?'

raw: Apparently not, for he became gloomy again.
en: Apparently not, as Carton became gloomy again.
ko: 카턴이 다시 우울해진 것을 보니 분명 그렇지 않은 것 같았다.

raw: “Pretty witness,” he muttered, looking down into his glass. “I have had enough of witnesses to-day and to-night; who’s your pretty witness?”
en: "The pretty witness," he muttered, looking at his glass. "I've seen enough witnesses today. Who do you mean?"
ko: '예쁜 증인이라,' 그가 잔을 바라보며 중얼거렸다. '오늘 증인은 볼 만큼 봤어. 누굴 말하는 거야?'

raw: “The picturesque doctor’s daughter, Miss Manette.”
en: "The doctor’s beautiful daughter, Miss Manette."
ko: '의사의 아름다운 딸, 마네트 양 말이야.'

raw: “_She_ pretty?”
en: "_She_ is pretty?"
ko: '그 여자가 예쁘다고?'

raw: “Is she not?”
en: "Is she not?"
ko: '그렇지 않은가?'

raw: “No.”
en: "No."
ko: '아니.'

raw: “Why, man alive, she was the admiration of the whole Court!”
en: "Why, everyone in the courtroom was admiring her!"
ko: '아니, 법정에 있던 모든 사람들이 그녀에게 감탄했다고!'

raw: “Rot the admiration of the whole Court!
en: "Who cares what the courtroom thinks?
ko: '법정 사람들이 어떻게 생각하든 무슨 상관이야?

raw: Who made the Old Bailey a judge of beauty?
en: Since when is the Old Bailey a judge of beauty?
ko: 올드 베일리가 언제부터 미의 기준이 되었지?

raw: She was a golden-haired doll!”
en: She's just a golden-haired doll!"
ko: 그녀는 그냥 금발 머리 인형일 뿐이야!'

raw: “Do you know, Sydney,” said Mr.
en: "Do you know, Sydney," Mr.
ko: '있지, 시드니,' 미스터

raw: Stryver, looking at him with sharp eyes, and slowly drawing a hand across his florid face: “do you know, I rather thought, at the time, that you sympathised with the golden-haired doll, and were quick to see what happened to the golden-haired doll?”
en: Stryver said, looking at him closely. "I actually thought you felt sorry for her. You were very quick to notice when she fainted."
ko: 스트라이버가 그를 유심히 바라보며 말했다. '난 사실 자네가 그녀를 가엾게 여긴다고 생각했어. 그녀가 기절했을 때 아주 재빨리 알아챘잖아.'

raw: “Quick to see what happened!
en: "Quick to notice!
ko: '재빨리 알아채다니!

raw: If a girl, doll or no doll, swoons within a yard or two of a man’s nose, he can see it without a perspective-glass.
en: If any girl faints right in front of a man's nose, he doesn't need glasses to see it.
ko: 어떤 여자든 남자 코앞에서 기절한다면, 그걸 보는 데 안경 따윈 필요 없지.

raw: I pledge you, but I deny the beauty.
en: I will drink to her, but I deny she is beautiful.
ko: 그녀를 위해 건배는 하겠지만, 그녀가 아름답다는 건 부인하겠어.

raw: And now I’ll have no more drink; I’ll get to bed.”
en: And now, no more drinking. I'm going to bed."
ko: 그리고 이제, 술은 그만. 난 자러 갈 거네."

raw: When his host followed him out on the staircase with a candle, to light him down the stairs, the day was coldly looking in through its grimy windows.
en: As Stryver walked him to the stairs with a candle, the cold morning light was beginning to show through the dirty windows.
ko: 스트라이버가 촛불을 들고 그를 계단까지 바래다주었을 때, 더러운 창문 너머로 차가운 아침 햇살이 비치기 시작하고 있었다.

raw: When he got out of the house, the air was cold and sad, the dull sky overcast, the river dark and dim, the whole scene like a lifeless desert.
en: Outside, the air was cold and gloomy, the sky gray, and the river dark, the whole city looked like a lifeless desert.
ko: 밖은 공기가 차갑고 음울했으며, 하늘은 잿빛이고 강은 어두워 도시 전체가 생명 없는 사막처럼 보였다.

raw: And wreaths of dust were spinning round and round before the morning blast, as if the desert-sand had risen far away, and the first spray of it in its advance had begun to overwhelm the city.
en: Swirls of dust were spinning round and round in the strong morning wind, looking as if desert sand had lifted up from far away and its first waves had just begun to bury the city.
ko: 강한 아침 바람에 먼지 소용돌이가 빙글빙글 돌고 있었는데, 마치 멀리서 사막의 모래가 솟아올라 그 첫 물결이 막 도시를 뒤덮기 시작한 것 같았다.

raw: Waste forces within him, and a desert all around, this man stood still on his way across a silent terrace, and saw for a moment, lying in the wilderness before him, a mirage of honourable ambition, self-denial, and perseverance.
en: With wasted potential inside him and a lonely desert all around him, the man stood completely still while crossing a quiet terrace. For a brief moment, he saw a mirage in the wasteland ahead of him: a vision of honorable ambition, self-control, and hard work.
ko: 그의 안에는 낭비된 잠재력이, 주변에는 외로운 사막만이 있는 채로, 그 남자는 고요한 테라스를 가로지르다 완전히 멈춰 섰다. 짧은 순간, 그는 눈앞의 황무지에서 신기루를 보았다. 그것은 명예로운 야망, 자제력, 그리고 노력의 환영이었다.

raw: In the fair city of this vision, there were airy galleries from which the loves and graces looked upon him, gardens in which the fruits of life hung ripening, waters of Hope that sparkled in his sight.
en: For a moment, he imagined a better life of honest ambition, self-control, and hard work. In that vision, he saw happiness, success, and hope.
ko: 잠시나마 그는 정직한 야망과 자제력, 그리고 노력으로 이루어진 더 나은 삶을 상상했다. 그 환영 속에서 그는 행복과 성공, 그리고 희망을 보았다.

raw: A moment, and it was gone.
en: A moment later, the vision vanished.
ko: 잠시 후, 그 환영은 사라졌다.

raw: Climbing to a high chamber in a well of houses, he threw himself down in his clothes on a neglected bed, and its pillow was wet with wasted tears.
en: Climbing the stairs to his dusty room, he threw himself onto his bed in his clothes and wept.
ko: 먼지 쌓인 자기 방으로 계단을 올라가, 그는 옷을 입은 채 침대에 몸을 던지고 눈물을 흘렸다.

raw: Sadly, sadly, the sun rose; it rose upon no sadder sight than the man of good abilities and good emotions, incapable of their directed exercise, incapable of his own help and his own happiness, sensible of the blight on him, and resigning himself to let it eat him away.
en: Sadly, the sun rose. It looked down on no sadder sight than this talented man. He was unable to use his abilities. He was unable to help himself or find happiness. He was fully aware of his wasted life and resigned to letting it ruin him.
ko: 슬프게도 해가 떠올랐다. 해는 이 재능 있는 남자보다 더 슬픈 광경을 내려다본 적이 없었다. 그는 자신의 능력을 쓸 수 없었다. 자신을 돕지도, 행복을 찾지도 못했다. 그는 자신의 낭비된 삶을 온전히 깨닫고 있었고, 그것이 자신을 파멸시키도록 내버려두기로 체념했다.
